entry.evidence: its crystallization mechanisms and relationship to fluid evolution in IOCG are poorly understood

sequences.source_document: Published PDF (body text) and publisher XML text (abstract, captions)

steps.action: Pose the question of how garnet crystallizes in IOCG systems and how it relates to fluid evolution and metamorphism, using the Yinachang deposit.
steps.quote: its crystallization mechanisms and relationship to fluid evolution in IOCG are poorly understood

steps.action: Describe the deposit geology, alteration zoning (breccia, proximal and intermediate K-Fe, distal Na) and four-stage paragenesis, combining earlier published work with new field and microscope observations.
steps.quote: the paragenesis of the Yinachang deposit has been described by Hou et al. (2013), Li et al. (2015) and Zhu et al. (2020)

steps.action: Record where garnet occurs: in stages 2-3, confined to alteration haloes near breccia bodies and dependent on host-rock type.
steps.quote: Garnet is common in the stage 2 and 3 of mineralization, and is strictly distributed in the alteration haloes within 200–500 m

steps.action: State the rival view from the regional survey report, which holds that the garnet-biotite-quartz rock formed during post-mineralization regional metamorphism, and set it against the limited distribution of garnet.
steps.quote: regional metamorphism (Regional Geological Survey Report of Wuding Area, RGSRW, 1992)

steps.action: Compare bulk-rock Fe/(Fe+Mg) and REE patterns of ore and alteration-zone samples with unaltered rocks (from the first author's thesis) to support an alteration origin for garnet, biotite and albite.
steps.quote: which are much higher than the unaltered rocks (0.68–0.70), consistent with the interpretation based on mineralogical observation.

steps.action: Design sampling with three garnet samples from each of the ore body, the proximal and the intermediate zones, and run microscopy and BSE imaging before analysis.
steps.quote: Three garnet samples from the Fe-Cu ore body (DFH-B4, DFH-B8, and DFH-B9)

steps.action: Calibrate EPMA against mineral standards and LA-ICP-MS against the NIST 612 and KL2-G reference glasses, and report detection limits and precision.
steps.quote: Data calibration was undertaken by analysis of National Institute of Standards (NIST) 612 glass and the USGS KL2-G standards.

steps.action: Classify three garnet types by location, colour, grain size, zoning and inclusions, and order their paragenesis (Grt 1 before Grt 2, Grt 3 last).
steps.quote: Three main types of garnets were recognized based on microscopy and BSE imaging

steps.action: Measure in situ major elements (EPMA) and trace elements and REE (LA-ICP-MS) at the same spots, with core-to-rim profiles and inter-element correlations for each garnet type.
steps.quote: All the garnets from the Yinachang deposit are Al-rich

steps.action: Derive crystal-chemical expectations for site occupancy of LILE, HFSE, U-Th and REE from ionic radii and substitution equations.
steps.quote: the ionic radius and charge mismatch between the host cation and its substituent, at a given site, exert the principal control on the substitution mechanisms

steps.action: Compare the measured LILE, U-Th, LREE and Eu behaviour with the crystal-chemical expectations and find mismatches, so equilibrium crystal chemistry alone cannot explain the compositions.
steps.quote: These differences suggests that the LILE contents cannot be simply attributed to the differences in ionic size

steps.action: Weigh distribution, mineral association, crosscutting veins and deformation, and interpret all garnets as hydrothermal and syn-mineralization.
steps.quote: to be formed by hydrothermal metasomatism during the mineralization

steps.action: Propose slow, near-equilibrium growth for zoned Grt 1 and rapid growth with surface adsorption for Grt 2 and Grt 3, based on grain size, inclusions and HREE preference.
steps.quote: The abundant inclusions in the Grt 3 also indicate high growth rates during metasomatism

steps.action: Adopt the earlier fluid model (magmatic-hydrothermal plus meteoric water, with mixing) and assign wall-rock and magmatic-fluid influence to Grt 1 and meteoric water to Grt 2-3.
steps.quote: Hou et al. (2013) and Li et al. (2015) claimed that the ore-forming fluids of the Yinachang deposit consisted of magmatic hydrothermal and meteoric waters

steps.action: Take expected REE signatures of magmatic-hydrothermal fluids and the solubility and complexation behaviour of LILE, HFSE and REE from experimental and thermodynamic literature.
steps.quote: magmatic hydrothermal typically have low ∑REE contents, are LREE-enriched and HREE-depleted, and have generally positive Eu anomalies

steps.action: Match the Grt 1 REE patterns to slow growth from a high-salinity magmatic fluid, and the Grt 3 LREE-depleted, high-∑REE patterns to lower-salinity meteoric water.
steps.quote: coresponding to the interpretation that these garnets grew slowly in a magmatic hydrothermal with a high salinity

steps.action: Infer, qualitatively, decreasing temperature and pressure from core-to-rim MgO, MnO and CaO trends, and reduced fO2 (below the hematite-magnetite buffer) from magnetite and sulfides and Eu behaviour.
steps.quote: Garnets from the Yinachang deposit display a general increase in MgO, and a decrease in MnO and CaO from core to rim

steps.action: Reuse the earlier bulk-rock data to argue strong wall-rock buffering for Grt 1 and Grt 2 and fluid control for Grt 3.
steps.quote: [...] buffering effect of wall rocks on the compositions of Grt 1 and Grt 2

steps.action: Keep the account that the Grt 1 to Grt 3 REE systematics record a shift from magmatic to meteoric fluid with falling T, P and fO2, and assert that low-grade metamorphism did not reset trace elements.
steps.quote: along with a decrease in temperature, pressure, and fO2

steps.action: Compile garnet characteristics from other IOCG deposits (Sin Quyen, Groundhog, Hillside, Nautanen) and compare them with Yinachang.
steps.quote: A comparison of garnet characteristics from global examples of IOCG deposits is shown in Table 6.

steps.action: State two rival origins for almandine in IOCG systems: Fe metasomatism of Al-rich pelite under reduced conditions, or Fe enrichment by alteration followed by post-ore metamorphism.
steps.quote: The pelitic protolith could be originally Fe enriched by alteration, and then metamorphosed by post-ore regional tectonic events which actually formed garnets.

steps.action: Reject post-ore metamorphic formation for the Yinachang garnets using their distribution, intergrowth, overprinting by stage-3 veins and deformation, and bulk composition.
steps.quote: These evidence are supportive for the synchroneity between garnets and alteration in the Yinachang Deposit.

steps.action: Conclude that almandine can be hydrothermal in IOCG deposits and could serve as a fluid-evolution and prospecting tool.
steps.quote: This study also suggests that almandine, which is generally considered to be of metamorphic origin, can have a hydrothermal origin in IOCG deposits.

steps.action: Leave the general almandine claim as a hypothesis for further garnet studies in other IOCG deposits.
steps.quote: Further mineralogical and geochemical studies of garnets in IOCG deposits should be conducted to test this hypothesis.

end.claim: Yinachang garnets are hydrothermal. Grt 1 and Grt 2 compositions reflect crystal-chemical substitution and wall-rock buffering during slow growth from magmatic-hydrothermal fluid. Grt 3 reflects surface adsorption during rapid growth from mixed magmatic and meteoric fluid. Falling T, P and fO2 account for the differences between the types.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the same-spot EPMA and LA-ICP-MS core-to-rim analyses of the three garnet types, none of the mechanism or fluid interpretations would exist.

gates.evidence: Sampling was stratified by alteration zone; no stated hypothesis directed acquisition. The crystal-chemical expectations could have matched the data and were reported as failing (p. 10, 13), but the preferred kinetic and fluid account was only matched qualitatively against cited behaviour, never against a stated test. Nothing was fixed before the data.

REE and HFSE complexation with F, Cl and OH in fluids
LA-ICP-MS (New Wave UP 213 laser coupled to a Thermo Element II)

This study also suggests that almandine, which is generally considered to be of metamorphic origin, can have a hydrothermal origin in IOCG deposits.

limits: The XML text supplied holds only the abstract and captions. Its abstract differs in wording from the PDF abstract; inference: it may be an earlier version, but no review file or version history was identified, so no review sequence was coded. Only nine samples from one open pit (Dongfanghong block) were analysed, and the garnet types are defined partly by sampling location. There is no statistical treatment of the correlations and no independent replication, alternative method or sensitivity test. The fluid model (magmatic plus meteoric mixing) is inherited from the authors' and others' earlier fluid-inclusion and isotope work, not tested here. The bulk-rock comparison with unaltered rocks comes from the first author's 2013 thesis. The claim that low-grade metamorphism did not reset trace elements is asserted, not tested (p. 21). T, P and fO2 trends are qualitative, with no thermobarometry. The paper names possible REE host minerals but does not quantify their effect (p. 17). Sub-claims: (a) hydrothermal, syn-ore origin of the Yinachang garnets, best_explanation; (b) decreasing T, P and fO2, best_explanation, qualitative; (c) almandine can be hydrothermal in IOCG deposits generally, none (proposed for testing, p. 23). Coder observation: in Table 4 the first five DFH-B1 spot analyses repeat the DFH-B9 values exactly, and some Table 3 DFH-B1 end-member columns look shifted; the paper does not comment on either. Data are available only on request. The comparison with other IOCG deposits (Table 6) uses literature data and is not coded as a check of the Yinachang result.

disagreements.support: Garnet is confined to alteration haloes around the deposit and is absent from carbonate and unaltered Yinmin rocks; it is intergrown with alteration minerals and overprinted by stage-3 veins; and garnet-bearing rocks have a distinct bulk composition.

disagreements.target: General view that almandine forms mainly during metamorphism (Chinner, 1962; Pan and Wan, 1993; Zhao et al., 2011)
disagreements.support: The hydrothermal setting and syn-ore relations at Yinachang and other IOCG deposits, plus reduced fO2, are argued to allow hydrothermal almandine.
disagreements.quote: This study also suggests that almandine, which is generally considered to be of metamorphic origin, can have a hydrothermal origin in IOCG deposits.
